10.5.s: agnaye pathikṛte 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yasya paurṇamāsī vāmāvasyā vātipadyeta bahiṣpathaṃ vā eṣa eti yasya paurṇamāsī vāmāvasyā vātipadyate | agnir devānāṃ pathikṛt tam evānvārabhate sa enaṃ panthām apinayati vi vā etad yajñaṃ chinatti yad yajñe pratata etām antareṣṭiṃ nirvapati ya evāsā āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ pūrṇamāse yo 'māvasyāyāṃ tam agnaye pathikṛte kuryāt tenaiva punaḥ panthām avaiti na yajñaṃ vicchinatti | agnaye vājasṛte 'ṣṭāpakālaṃ nirvapet saṃgrāme | agnir vai devānāṃ vājasṛt | vājam eṣa dhāvati yas saṃgrāmaṃ jayati tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati vājam eva dhāvati jayati saṃgrāmam atho agnir iva na pratidhṛṣe bhavati | agnaye vratapataye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped ya āhitāgnis sann avratyaṃ caret | ānīto vā eṣa devānāṃ ya āhitāgnir adanty asyānnam | vratapatim etasya vrataṃ gacchati ya āhitāgnis sann avratyaṃ carati | agnir devānāṃ vratapatis tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati vratapater evādhi vratam ālabhate | agnaye rakṣoghne 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped āmayāvī | indraṃ vai jātaṃ rakṣāṃsy asacanta sa ādīyamāno rakṣobhis saṃmṛśyamāno 'gniṃ prāviśat tasmād agnī rakṣāṃsy apāhan rakṣāṃsy etaṃ sacante ya āmayāvī | agnir devānāṃ rakṣohā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smād rakṣāṃsy apahanti | amāvasyāṃ rātrīṃ niśi yajeta | amāvasyāṃ vai rātrīṃ niśi rakṣāṃsi prerate prerṇāny evaināny apavapati pariśrite yajeta rakṣasāmantarhityai | vāmadevasyaitat pañcadaśaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ sāmidhenyo bhavanti vāmadevaś ca vai kusidāyī cātmanor ājim ayātām | tasya kusidāyī pūrvasyātidrutasya kūbaraṃ nyamṛṇat sā dvitīyam upaparyāvartateṣāṃ vākṣaṃ vā chetsyāsīti sa vāmadeva ukhyam agnim abibhar | tam avaikṣata sa etat sūktam apaśyat kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīm iti tām agnir anūddrutya samadahat sā dahyamānā hradaṃ kausidaṃ prāmajjat | yad etad anūcyate rakṣasāṃ duṣṭyai |
10.5.d: अग्नये पथिकृते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यस्य पौर्णमासी वामावस्या वातिपद्येत बहिष्पथं वा एष एति यस्य पौर्णमासी वामावस्या वातिपद्यते । अग्निर् देवानां पथिकृत् तम् एवान्वारभते स एनं पन्थाम् अपिनयति वि वा एतद् यज्ञं छिनत्ति यद् यज्ञे प्रतत एताम् अन्तरेष्टिं निर्वपति य एवासा आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः पूर्णमासे यो ऽमावस्यायां तम् अग्नये पथिकृते कुर्यात् तेनैव पुनः पन्थाम् अवैति न यज्ञं विच्छिनत्ति । अग्नये वाजसृते ऽष्टापकालं निर्वपेत् संग्रामे । अग्निर् वै देवानां वाजसृत् । वाजम् एष धावति यस् संग्रामं जयति तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति वाजम् एव धावति जयति संग्रामम् अथो अग्निर् इव न प्रतिधृषे भवति । अग्नये व्रतपतये ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् य आहिताग्निस् सन्न् अव्रत्यं चरेत् । आनीतो वा एष देवानां य आहिताग्निर् अदन्त्य् अस्यान्नम् । व्रतपतिम् एतस्य व्रतं गच्छति य आहिताग्निस् सन्न् अव्रत्यं चरति । अग्निर् देवानां व्रतपतिस् तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति व्रतपतेर् एवाधि व्रतम् आलभते । अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् आमयावी । इन्द्रं वै जातं रक्षांस्य् असचन्त स आदीयमानो रक्षोभिस् संमृश्यमानो ऽग्निं प्राविशत् तस्माद् अग्नी रक्षांस्य् अपाहन् रक्षांस्य् एतं सचन्ते य आमयावी । अग्निर् देवानां रक्षोहा तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्माद् रक्षांस्य् अपहन्ति । अमावस्यां रात्रीं निशि यजेत । अमावस्यां वै रात्रीं निशि रक्षांसि प्रेरते प्रेर्णान्य् एवैनान्य् अपवपति परिश्रिते यजेत रक्षसामन्तर्हित्यै । वामदेवस्यैतत् पञ्चदशं रक्षोघ्नं सामिधेन्यो भवन्ति वामदेवश् च वै कुसिदायी चात्मनोर् आजिम् अयाताम् । तस्य कुसिदायी पूर्वस्यातिद्रुतस्य कूबरं न्यमृणत् सा द्वितीयम् उपपर्यावर्ततेषां वाक्षं वा छेत्स्यासीति स वामदेव उख्यम् अग्निम् अबिभर् । तम् अवैक्षत स एतत् सूक्तम् अपश्यत् कृणुष्व पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीम् इति ताम् अग्निर् अनूद्द्रुत्य समदहत् सा दह्यमाना ह्रदं कौसिदं प्रामज्जत् । यद् एतद् अनूच्यते रक्षसां दुष्ट्यै ।
10.5.m:
One whose full-moon day or new-moon day should be missed should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt.
He goes off the path whose full-moon day or new-moon day is missed.
Agni is the path-maker of the gods.
He takes hold of him;
he leads him back to the path.
He cuts the sacrifice asunder when, while the sacrifice is extended, he performs this intermediate offering.
That cake on eight potsherds to Agni which is at the full moon [or] that which is at the new moon, he should make that for Agni Pathikṛt.
By that he goes down again to the path;
he does not cut the sacrifice asunder.
In battle, he should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vājasṛt.
Agni is the prize-runner among the gods.
He runs for the prize who wins a battle.
He runs up to him with his share;
he runs for the prize;
he wins the battle;
moreover, like Agni, he becomes unassailable.
One who has consecrated fires but acts contrary to his vows should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati.
He who has consecrated fires has been brought near to the gods;
they eat his food.
The vow of him who has consecrated fires but acts contrary to his vows goes away to the lord of vows.
Agni is the lord of vows among the gods.
He runs up to him with his share;
he takes back his vow from the lord of vows.
A sick man should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Rakṣohan.
When Indra was born, the demons pursued him.
He, being seized and touched on all sides by the demons, entered Agni.
Therefore Agni struck away the demons.
The demons pursue him who is sick.
Agni is the demon-slayer among the gods.
He runs up to him with his share;
he strikes away the demons from him.
He should sacrifice at night on the new-moon night.
At night on the new-moon night the demons set forth.
He casts them away just as they have set forth.
He should sacrifice in an enclosed space,
for the concealment of the demons.
There are these fifteen demon-slaying sāmidhenī verses of Vāmadeva.
Vāmadeva and Kusidāyī ran a race between themselves.
Kusidāyī broke the pole of his [chariot] as he ran ahead first.
She turned round towards him a second time, [thinking:] "I will break the pole or the axle of the chariot!"
That Vāmadeva was carrying the fire in the pan.
He looked down upon it;
he saw this hymn:
"Display your vigor like an expansive net!"
Running after her, Agni burned her thoroughly.
Being burned, she plunged into the pool of Kusīda.
Because this is recited,
[it is] for the spoiling of the demons.

10.6.s: naimiṣyā vai sattram āsata ta utthāya saptaviṃśatiṃ kurupañcāleṣu vatsatarān avanvata tān vako dālbhir abravīt | yūyam evaitān vibhajadhvam imam ahaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ vaicitravīryaṃ gamiṣyāmi sa mahyaṃ gṛhān kariṣyatīti tam āgacchat tan nāsūrkṣat taṃ prākālayata | etā gā brahmabandha iti | abravīt paśupatir gā hanti tāḥ paraḥ pacamānaś careti tāsāṃ devasūr me rājānnaṃ prāsuṣod iti sakthāny utkartam apacata tasmin pacamāne vyadasyat so 'gnaye rudravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapat kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇām | tasya yat kiṃca dhṛtarāṣṭrasyāsīt tat sarvam avakīrṇaṃ vidrāṇam abhi vyaucchat tā vipraśnikā avindan brāhmaṇo vai tvāyam abhicarati tasminnāthasveti tam upāśikṣat tasmai bahv adadāt so 'gnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapac chuklānāṃ vrīhīṇām | tato vai tad vyadasyat | agnaye rudravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇām abhicaran | agnir vai rudras | rudrāyaivainam apidadhāti kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ bhavati kṛṣṇam iva vai tamas tamo mṛtyus | mṛtyunaivainaṃ grahayati | agnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yarhy ayaṃ devaḥ prajā abhimanyeta yadā kāmayeta vidasyed iti | eṣā vā agner bhiṣajyā tanūr yā surabhimatī tām eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tayainā bhiṣajyati | agnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yam apramītaṃ pramītaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ pūtir vā eṣa śrūyate yaḥ pramītaś śrūyate yaivāgnes surabhimatī tanūs tām eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tayainaṃ surabhiṃ karoti | agnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yam ajaghnivāṃsam abhiśaṃseyus | śamalagṛhīto vā eṣa yam ajaghnivāṃsam abhiśaṃsanti yaivāgnes surabhimatī tanūs tām eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tayainaṃ punāti | agnaye 'nnādāyāṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayetānnādas syām iti | agnir vai devānām annādas tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam annādaṃ karoti | agnaye 'nnavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayetānnavān syām iti | agnir vai devānāṃ annavān | tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam annavantaṃ karoti | agnaye 'nnapataye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayetānnapatis syām iti | agnir vai devānām annapatis tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam annapatiṃ karoti saṃvatsaraṃ parinirvapet saṃvatsaro vā annādyasya pradātā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam annādam annavantam annapatiṃ karoti | agnaye vasumate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo brāhmaṇas | yad vai kiṃca vindate tad vasu | agnir devānāṃ vasumān | tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smai sarvān kāmān prayacchati |
10.6.d: नैमिष्या वै सत्त्रम् आसत त उत्थाय सप्तविंशतिं कुरुपञ्चालेषु वत्सतरान् अवन्वत तान् वको दाल्भिर् अब्रवीत् । यूयम् एवैतान् विभजध्वम् इमम् अहं धृतराष्ट्रं वैचित्रवीर्यं गमिष्यामि स मह्यं गृहान् करिष्यतीति तम् आगच्छत् तन् नासूर्क्षत् तं प्राकालयत । एता गा ब्रह्मबन्ध इति । अब्रवीत् पशुपतिर् गा हन्ति ताः परः पचमानश् चरेति तासां देवसूर् मे राजान्नं प्रासुषोद् इति सक्थान्य् उत्कर्तम् अपचत तस्मिन् पचमाने व्यदस्यत् सो ऽग्नये रुद्रवते ऽष्टाकपालं निरवपत् कृष्णानां व्रीहीणाम् । तस्य यत् किंच धृतराष्ट्रस्यासीत् तत् सर्वम् अवकीर्णं विद्राणम् अभि व्यौच्छत् ता विप्रश्निका अविन्दन् ब्राह्मणो वै त्वायम् अभिचरति तस्मिन्नाथस्वेति तम् उपाशिक्षत् तस्मै बह्व् अददात् सो ऽग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निरवपच् छुक्लानां व्रीहीणाम् । ततो वै तद् व्यदस्यत् । अग्नये रुद्रवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् कृष्णानां व्रीहीणाम् अभिचरन् । अग्निर् वै रुद्रस् । रुद्रायैवैनम् अपिदधाति कृष्णानां व्रीहीणां भवति कृष्णम् इव वै तमस् तमो मृत्युस् । मृत्युनैवैनं ग्रहयति । अग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यर्ह्य् अयं देवः प्रजा अभिमन्येत यदा कामयेत विदस्येद् इति । एषा वा अग्नेर् भिषज्या तनूर् या सुरभिमती ताम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति तयैना भिषज्यति । अग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यम् अप्रमीतं प्रमीतं शृणुयुः पूतिर् वा एष श्रूयते यः प्रमीतश् श्रूयते यैवाग्नेस् सुरभिमती तनूस् ताम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति तयैनं सुरभिं करोति । अग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यम् अजघ्निवांसम् अभिशंसेयुस् । शमलगृहीतो वा एष यम् अजघ्निवांसम् अभिशंसन्ति यैवाग्नेस् सुरभिमती तनूस् ताम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति तयैनं पुनाति । अग्नये ऽन्नादायाष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेतान्नादस् स्याम् इति । अग्निर् वै देवानाम् अन्नादस् तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अन्नादं करोति । अग्नये ऽन्नवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेतान्नवान् स्याम् इति । अग्निर् वै देवानां अन्नवान् । तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अन्नवन्तं करोति । अग्नये ऽन्नपतये ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेतान्नपतिस् स्याम् इति । अग्निर् वै देवानाम् अन्नपतिस् तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अन्नपतिं करोति संवत्सरं परिनिर्वपेत् संवत्सरो वा अन्नाद्यस्य प्रदाता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अन्नादम् अन्नवन्तम् अन्नपतिं करोति । अग्नये वसुमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् सर्वेभ्यः कामेभ्यो ब्राह्मणस् । यद् वै किंच विन्दते तद् वसु । अग्निर् देवानां वसुमान् । तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मै सर्वान् कामान् प्रयच्छति ।

10.7.s: agnaye yaviṣṭhāyāṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped abhicaran vābhicaryamāṇo vā devāś ca vā asurāś ca vyabhyacaranta te 'surā devebhyo visṛṣṭīr vyasṛjan | te devā avidur visṛṣṭīr vai no 'surā vyasrākṣur iti te 'gnaye yaviṣṭhāyāṣṭākapālaṃ niravapan | tena vai te tā visṛṣṭīr ayāvayantātmano 'dhi visṛṣṭim etasmai visṛjanti yam abhicaranti yad agnaye yaviṣṭhāya nirvapati tenaiva tāṃ visṛṣṭiṃ yāvayata ātmano 'dhi | agnaye yaviṣṭhāyāṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet samṛtasome devatāsu vā ete samṛcchante yeṣāṃ somau samṛcchete agnis sarvā devatās | agninaivaiṣāṃ yaviṣṭhena devatā vṛṅkte | devāś ca vā asurāś ca saṃyattā āsan yān devānām aghnaṃs tad eva te 'bhavan yān asurāṇāṃ punas ta utpattyāyudhyanta te devā avidur ye vai na ime keca mriyante 'gnir vāvaitān hantīti te 'bruvan mā naś śamnīthāḥ kathā naś śamnīṣa iti bhāgo me 'stv ity abravīt | na vo 'bhāgadheyaḥ kṣamiṣya iti te 'gnaye kṣamavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapan | tato vai sa tebhyo 'kṣamata | agnaye kṣamavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yarhy ayaṃ devaḥ prajā abhimanyeta yadā kāmayeta vidasyed iti ye vā ime keca mriyante 'gnir vāvaitān hanti | agnir devānāṃ kṣamavān | tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smai prītaḥ kṣamata eva devāḥ pitaro manuṣyās te 'nyata āsann asurā rakṣāṃsi piśācās te 'nyatas te samayatanta te yad devānām apy alpakaṃ lohitam asurā akurvan | tad rātrībhī rakṣāṃsy asumbhan | tān subdhān mṛtān abhi vyaucchat te devā avidur ye vai na ime keca mriyante rakṣāṃsi vāvaitān sumbhantīti tāny upāmantrayanta tāny abruvan vāryaṃ vṛṇāmahai yad evemān asurāñ jayāma tan nas sahāsad iti tato devā asurān ajayan | te 'surāñ jitvā rakṣāṃsy apānudanta tāny anṛtam akarteti samantaṃ devān paryaviśan | te devā agnā evānāthanta te 'gnaye pravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapann agnaye vibādhavate 'ṣṭākapālam agnaye pratīkavate 'ṣṭākapālam | yad agnaye pravate yāny eva purastād rakṣāṃsy āsaṃs tāni tena prāṇudanta yad vibādhavate yāny evābhita āsaṃs tāni tena vyabhādanta yat pratīkavate yāny eva paścād rakṣāṃsy āsaṃs tāni tenāpānudanta | etayā yajeta bhrātṛvyavān yo bahubhrātṛvyas syāt | agnaye pravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped agnaye vibādhavate 'ṣṭākapālam agnaye pratīkavate 'ṣṭākapālam | yad agnaye pravate ya evainaṃ pūrvo 'tikrānto bhrātṛvyas taṃ tena praṇudate yad vibādhavate ya evainena sadṛṅ taṃ tena vibādhate yat pratīkavate ya evāsya paścād bhrātṛvyas taṃ tenāpanudate pra śreyāṃsaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ nudate 'ti sadṛśaṃ krāmati nainaṃ pāpīyān āpnoti ya evaṃ vidvān etayā yajate devāś ca vā asurāś ca saṃyattā āsan | tān gāyatry antarātiṣṭhat | ojo vīryam annādyaṃ parigṛhya saṃvatsaro vāvainān so 'ntarātiṣṭhat | caturviṃśatir gāyatryā akṣarāṇi caturviṃśatis saṃvatsarasyārdhamāsās te 'vidur yatarān vā iyam upāvartsyati ta idaṃ bhaviṣyantīti tāṃ vyahvayanta dābhīty asurā ahvayan viśvakarmann iti devās sā nānyatarāṃścanopāvartata te devā etad yajur apaśyan | ojo 'si saho 'si balam asi bhrājo 'si devānāṃ dhāma nāmāsi viśvam asi viśvāyus sarvam asi sarvāyur abhibhūr iti sā devān upāvartata tato devā abhavan parāsurā abhavan | āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped bhrātṛvyavān vā spardhamāno vā tam āsādyaitair yajurbhir abhimṛśet | ojo vai vīryaṃ saṃvatsaras | oja eva vīryaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte sa nirvīryaḥ parābhavati saiṣā gāyatrī nāmeṣṭis | atho āhuḥ kṣatrasya saṃvarga iti |
10.7.d: अग्नये यविष्ठायाष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् अभिचरन् वाभिचर्यमाणो वा देवाश् च वा असुराश् च व्यभ्यचरन्त ते ऽसुरा देवेभ्यो विसृष्टीर् व्यसृजन् । ते देवा अविदुर् विसृष्टीर् वै नो ऽसुरा व्यस्राक्षुर् इति ते ऽग्नये यविष्ठायाष्टाकपालं निरवपन् । तेन वै ते ता विसृष्टीर् अयावयन्तात्मनो ऽधि विसृष्टिम् एतस्मै विसृजन्ति यम् अभिचरन्ति यद् अग्नये यविष्ठाय निर्वपति तेनैव तां विसृष्टिं यावयत आत्मनो ऽधि । अग्नये यविष्ठायाष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् समृतसोमे देवतासु वा एते समृच्छन्ते येषां सोमौ समृच्छेते अग्निस् सर्वा देवतास् । अग्निनैवैषां यविष्ठेन देवता वृङ्क्ते । देवाश् च वा असुराश् च संयत्ता आसन् यान् देवानाम् अघ्नंस् तद् एव ते ऽभवन् यान् असुराणां पुनस् त उत्पत्त्यायुध्यन्त ते देवा अविदुर् ये वै न इमे केच म्रियन्ते ऽग्निर् वावैतान् हन्तीति ते ऽब्रुवन् मा नश् शम्नीथाः कथा नश् शम्नीष इति भागो मे ऽस्त्व् इत्य् अब्रवीत् । न वो ऽभागधेयः क्षमिष्य इति ते ऽग्नये क्षमवते ऽष्टाकपालं निरवपन् । ततो वै स तेभ्यो ऽक्षमत । अग्नये क्षमवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यर्ह्य् अयं देवः प्रजा अभिमन्येत यदा कामयेत विदस्येद् इति ये वा इमे केच म्रियन्ते ऽग्निर् वावैतान् हन्ति । अग्निर् देवानां क्षमवान् । तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मै प्रीतः क्षमत एव देवाः पितरो मनुष्यास् ते ऽन्यत आसन्न् असुरा रक्षांसि पिशाचास् ते ऽन्यतस् ते समयतन्त ते यद् देवानाम् अप्य् अल्पकं लोहितम् असुरा अकुर्वन् । तद् रात्रीभी रक्षांस्य् असुम्भन् । तान् सुब्धान् मृतान् अभि व्यौच्छत् ते देवा अविदुर् ये वै न इमे केच म्रियन्ते रक्षांसि वावैतान् सुम्भन्तीति तान्य् उपामन्त्रयन्त तान्य् अब्रुवन् वार्यं वृणामहै यद् एवेमान् असुराञ् जयाम तन् नस् सहासद् इति ततो देवा असुरान् अजयन् । ते ऽसुराञ् जित्वा रक्षांस्य् अपानुदन्त तान्य् अनृतम् अकर्तेति समन्तं देवान् पर्यविशन् । ते देवा अग्ना एवानाथन्त ते ऽग्नये प्रवते ऽष्टाकपालं निरवपन्न् अग्नये विबाधवते ऽष्टाकपालम् अग्नये प्रतीकवते ऽष्टाकपालम् । यद् अग्नये प्रवते यान्य् एव पुरस्ताद् रक्षांस्य् आसंस् तानि तेन प्राणुदन्त यद् विबाधवते यान्य् एवाभित आसंस् तानि तेन व्यभादन्त यत् प्रतीकवते यान्य् एव पश्चाद् रक्षांस्य् आसंस् तानि तेनापानुदन्त । एतया यजेत भ्रातृव्यवान् यो बहुभ्रातृव्यस् स्यात् । अग्नये प्रवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् अग्नये विबाधवते ऽष्टाकपालम् अग्नये प्रतीकवते ऽष्टाकपालम् । यद् अग्नये प्रवते य एवैनं पूर्वो ऽतिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेन प्रणुदते यद् विबाधवते य एवैनेन सदृङ् तं तेन विबाधते यत् प्रतीकवते य एवास्य पश्चाद् भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेनापनुदते प्र श्रेयांसं भ्रातृव्यं नुदते ऽति सदृशं क्रामति नैनं पापीयान् आप्नोति य एवं विद्वान् एतया यजते देवाश् च वा असुराश् च संयत्ता आसन् । तान् गायत्र्य् अन्तरातिष्ठत् । ओजो वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं परिगृह्य संवत्सरो वावैनान् सो ऽन्तरातिष्ठत् । चतुर्विंशतिर् गायत्र्या अक्षराणि चतुर्विंशतिस् संवत्सरस्यार्धमासास् ते ऽविदुर् यतरान् वा इयम् उपावर्त्स्यति त इदं भविष्यन्तीति तां व्यह्वयन्त दाभीत्य् असुरा अह्वयन् विश्वकर्मन्न् इति देवास् सा नान्यतरांश्चनोपावर्तत ते देवा एतद् यजुर् अपश्यन् । ओजो ऽसि सहो ऽसि बलम् असि भ्राजो ऽसि देवानां धाम नामासि विश्वम् असि विश्वायुस् सर्वम् असि सर्वायुर् अभिभूर् इति सा देवान् उपावर्तत ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा अभवन् । आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् भ्रातृव्यवान् वा स्पर्धमानो वा तम् आसाद्यैतैर् यजुर्भिर् अभिमृशेत् । ओजो वै वीर्यं संवत्सरस् । ओज एव वीर्यं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते स निर्वीर्यः पराभवति सैषा गायत्री नामेष्टिस् । अथो आहुः क्षत्रस्य संवर्ग इति ।
10.7.m:
One should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Yaviṣṭha when practicing sorcery or when being practiced upon with sorcery.
The gods and the Asuras were contending with each other by sorcery.
Those Asuras cast discharges against the gods.
Those gods knew: "The Asuras have indeed cast discharges against us."
They offered a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Yaviṣṭha.
By that, indeed, they warded off those discharges from themselves.
A discharge they cast against him whom they practice sorcery upon.
When he offers to Agni Yaviṣṭha,
by that indeed he wards off that discharge from himself.
One should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Yaviṣṭha at [an occasion when one is] one who has an equal Soma sacrifice.
In respect of the deities, indeed, they clash whose two Soma [sacrifices] clash.
Agni is all the deities.
By means of Agni Yaviṣṭha he appropriates their deities.
The gods and the Asuras were engaged in conflict.
Those of the gods whom they killed, there they remained;
those of the Asuras [whom they killed], rising up again, they fought.
Those gods knew: "Whoever among us here die, Agni indeed kills them."
They said: "Do not crush us! How do you crush us?"
"Let there be a portion for me!" he said,
"Without a portion I will not be patient with you."
They offered a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kṣamavat.
Thereupon, indeed, he was patient with them.
One should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kṣamavat when this god should threaten his creatures, [or] when he should desire: "May [the kingdom] dry up!"
Whoever among these die, Agni indeed kills them.
Agni is the patient one among the gods.
He approaches him with his portion;
he, pleased with him,
is indeed patient.
The gods, the fathers, [and] men were on one side; the Asuras, the Rakṣases, [and] the Piśācas were on the other side.
They clashed.
When the Asuras drew even a little blood from the gods,
then the Rakṣases crushed [them] by night.
Dawn shone upon them crushed [and] dead.
Those gods knew: "Whoever among us here die, the Rakṣases indeed crush them."
They addressed them.
They said: "Let us choose a boon: whatever we conquer from these Asuras, let that be ours together [with you]!"
Thereupon the gods conquered the Asuras.
Having conquered the Asuras, they repelled the Rakṣases.
Saying, "You have acted falsely!" they surrounded the gods on all sides.
Those gods sought shelter right in Agni.
They offered a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pravat, a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vibādhavat, [and] a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pratīkavat.
In that [he offers] to Agni Pravat, whatever Rakṣases were in front, those they drove forward with that.
In that [he offers] to Vibādhavat, whatever were on both sides, those they drove apart with that.
In that [he offers] to Pratīkavat, whatever Rakṣases were behind, those they drove back with that.
One who has a rival, who might have many rivals, should sacrifice with this [offering].
He should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pravat, a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vibādhavat, [and] a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pratīkavat.
In that [he offers] to Agni Pravat,
whatever rival has previously surpassed him, him he drives forward with that.
In that [he offers] to Vibādhavat,
whatever [rival] is equal to him, him he drives apart with that.
In that [he offers] to Pratīkavat,
whatever rival is behind him, him he drives back with that.
He pushes forward the superior rival; he steps beyond the equal;
a worse [rival] does not reach him who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this [offering].
The gods and the Asuras were engaged in conflict.
The Gāyatrī stood between them,
having encompassed power, virility, and proper food; or rather, the year stood between them.
Twenty-four are the syllables of the Gāyatrī;
twenty-four are the half-months of the year.
They knew: "Whichever of the two she will turn to, they will become this [all]."
They called to her.
"O Dābhī!" the Asuras called;
"O Viśvakarman!" the gods [called].
She turned to neither of the two.
Those gods saw this Yajus-formula:
"You are power; you are force; you are strength; you are radiance; you are the domain of the gods; you are name; you are the universe; you are full lifespan; you are all; you are complete lifespan; you are overcoming!"
She turned to the gods.
Thereupon the gods prospered, the Asuras were defeated.
One who has a rival or one who is competing should offer [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni.
Having placed it, he should touch it with these Yajus-formulas.
The year is power and virility.
He appropriates the power and virility of his rival;
he, deprived of virility, is defeated.
This same offering is called Gāyatrī;
and they also say: "The gathering-in of dominion."

10.8.s: indrāya gharmavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmas | asau vā ādityo gharmas | eṣa indras | eṣa brahmavarcasasya pradātā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smai brahmavarcasaṃ prayacchati | indrāyendriyavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet paśukāmas | indriyaṃ vai paśavas | indraḥ paśūnāṃ pradātā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smai paśūn prayacchati | indrāyārkavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped annakāmas | annaṃ vā arkas | indro 'nnādyasya pradātā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smā annādyaṃ prayacchati | indrāyārkavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped aparuddho 'vagamakāmas | antaṃ vā eṣa gacchati yam aparundhanti | eṣendrasyāntyā tanūr yārkavatī | anta evāsmā antaṃ kalpayati vaśā dakṣiṇā vaśaṃ mā nayād iti | indrāya gharmavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped indrāyendriyavata ekādaśakapālam indrāyārkavata ekādaśakapālaṃ samānabarhīṃṣi bubhūṣan yad indrāya gharmavate | asau vā ādityo gharmas | eṣa indras | eṣa śiraḥ prajānām | śira eva tena kurute yad indrāyendriyavate | indriyam eva tenātman dhatte yad indrāyārkavate | iyaṃ vā arkas | asyām eva tena pratitiṣṭhati carur madhye syāt | ajāmitvāya | indrāya manyumata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet saṃgrāme manyunā vai vīryaṃ karotīndriyeṇa jayati manyuṃ caivaiṣv indriyaṃ ca jityai dadhāti | indrāya manyumate manasvata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet saṃgrāme manyunā vai vīryaṃ karotīndriyeṇa jayati manuṃ caivaiṣv indriyaṃ ca sayujau kṛtvā tayor mano jityai dadhāti | indrāya manasvate tviṣīmata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayeta manasvī tviṣīmān syām iti mano vai śrīs tviṣis | mana evāsmiñ chriyaṃ tviṣiṃ dadhāti saṃvatsaraṃ purā manaso na kīrtayet saṃvatsareṇa vā anāptam āpyate saṃvatsaram evāptvāvarunddhe |
10.8.d: इन्द्राय घर्मवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस् । असौ वा आदित्यो घर्मस् । एष इन्द्रस् । एष ब्रह्मवर्चसस्य प्रदाता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मै ब्रह्मवर्चसं प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेत् पशुकामस् । इन्द्रियं वै पशवस् । इन्द्रः पशूनां प्रदाता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मै पशून् प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रायार्कवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् अन्नकामस् । अन्नं वा अर्कस् । इन्द्रो ऽन्नाद्यस्य प्रदाता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मा अन्नाद्यं प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रायार्कवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् अपरुद्धो ऽवगमकामस् । अन्तं वा एष गच्छति यम् अपरुन्धन्ति । एषेन्द्रस्यान्त्या तनूर् यार्कवती । अन्त एवास्मा अन्तं कल्पयति वशा दक्षिणा वशं मा नयाद् इति । इन्द्राय घर्मवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवत एकादशकपालम् इन्द्रायार्कवत एकादशकपालं समानबर्हींषि बुभूषन् यद् इन्द्राय घर्मवते । असौ वा आदित्यो घर्मस् । एष इन्द्रस् । एष शिरः प्रजानाम् । शिर एव तेन कुरुते यद् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवते । इन्द्रियम् एव तेनात्मन् धत्ते यद् इन्द्रायार्कवते । इयं वा अर्कस् । अस्याम् एव तेन प्रतितिष्ठति चरुर् मध्ये स्यात् । अजामित्वाय । इन्द्राय मन्युमत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेत् संग्रामे मन्युना वै वीर्यं करोतीन्द्रियेण जयति मन्युं चैवैष्व् इन्द्रियं च जित्यै दधाति । इन्द्राय मन्युमते मनस्वत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेत् संग्रामे मन्युना वै वीर्यं करोतीन्द्रियेण जयति मनुं चैवैष्व् इन्द्रियं च सयुजौ कृत्वा तयोर् मनो जित्यै दधाति । इन्द्राय मनस्वते त्विषीमत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेत मनस्वी त्विषीमान् स्याम् इति मनो वै श्रीस् त्विषिस् । मन एवास्मिञ् छ्रियं त्विषिं दधाति संवत्सरं पुरा मनसो न कीर्तयेत् संवत्सरेण वा अनाप्तम् आप्यते संवत्सरम् एवाप्त्वावरुन्द्धे ।
10.8.m:
One who desires spiritual luster should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Gharmavat.
Yonder sun is the gharma.
This is Indra.
He is the bestower of spiritual luster.
He approaches him with his share;
he grants him spiritual luster.
One who desires domestic animals should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Indriyavat.
Domestic animals are sensory power.
Indra is the bestower of domestic animals.
He approaches him with his share;
he grants him domestic animals.
One who desires food should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Arkavat.
Arka is food.
Indra is the bestower of proper food.
He approaches him with his share;
he grants him proper food.
One who is expelled and desires reinstatement should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Arkavat.
He goes to the end whom they expel.
This is Indra's final body, which is Arkavatī.
At the end he prepares an end for him.
A barren cow is the sacrificial fee,
[thinking:] "May it bring [him] into my control."
One who desires to become [prosperous] should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Gharmavat, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Indriyavat, and a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Arkavat, upon the same sacrificial grass.
In that [there is one] for Indra Gharmavat:
yonder sun is the gharma;
this is Indra;
he is the head of creatures;
he makes a head by that.
In that [there is one] for Indra Indriyavat:
he places sensory power in himself by that.
In that [there is one] for Indra Arkavat:
this [earth] is the arka;
he establishes himself on this [earth] by that.
There should be a mess of boiled grain in the middle,
for non-slackness.
In battle, one should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Manyumat.
By fury he performs heroic deed, by sensory power he wins;
he places fury and sensory power in them for victory.
In battle, one should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Manyumat Manasvat.
By fury he performs heroic deed, by sensory power he wins;
having yoked fury and sensory power together in them, he places the mind of the two for victory.
One who should desire, "May I be full of mind and full of brilliance," should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Manasvat Tviṣīmat.
Mind is fortune and brilliance.
He places mind, fortune, and brilliance in him.
He should not utter it for a year prior to the mind.
By a year what is unobtained is obtained.
Having obtained the year, he secures [it].

10.9.s: indrāya sutrāmṇa ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped aparuddho vāparurutsyamāno vā | indro vai trātendro 'paroddhā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enaṃ trāyate | indrāyāṃhomuca ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped āmayāvī | aṃhasā vā eṣa gṛhīto ya āmayāvī | eṣendrasya bhiṣajyā tanūr yāṃhomuk | indro 'ṃhaso moktā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam aṃhaso muñcati | indrāyāṃhomuca ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped ya ātmanā vā gṛhair vāṃhūraṇam aveyāt | aṃhasā vā eṣa gṛhīto ya ātmanā vā gṛhair vāṃhūraṇam avaiti | indro 'ṃhaso moktā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa enam aṃhaso muñcati | indrāyārkavate 'śvamedhavata ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayeta mahāyajño mopanamed iti | iyaṃ vā arko 'sā arkāsā aśvamedha aindro yajñas | antam etasya yajño gacchati yaṃ yajñakāmaṃ yajño nopanamati | ete indrasyāntye tanvau ye arkavatī ye evendrasyāntye tanvau tābhyām eva yajñam ālabhate | upainaṃ yajño namati | indrāyānvṛjava ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet sajātakāmas | indriyaṃ vai jyaiṣṭhyam indriyeṇaiva sajātān anvṛjūn kurute | indrāya prababhrāyaikādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped bhrātṛvyavān vajro vai prababhraḥ prababhreṇa vā indro 'surebhyo vajraṃ prāharat | vajram eva bhrātṛvyāya praharati stṛṇuta enam āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped indrāya vimṛdhāyaikādaśakapālaṃ saṃgrāme | ṛddhyā evāgneyas | indraṃ vai vṛtraṃ jaghnivāṃsaṃ mṛdho 'sacanta sa etaṃ vaimṛdham apaśyat tena tā mṛdho 'pāhata vṛtram eṣa jighāṃsati yas saṃgrāmaṃ jigīṣati yaivendrasya vimṛdhā tanūs tām eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tayā mṛdho 'pahate hanti vṛtram | jayati saṃgrāmam āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped indrāya vimṛdhāyaikādaśakapālaṃ yaṃ sarvato bhayam āgacchet | ṛddhyā evāgneyas | indraṃ vai vṛtraṃ jaghnivāṃsaṃ taṃ samantaṃ mṛdhas saṃprākampanta sa etaṃ vaimṛdham apaśyat tena tā mṛdho 'pāhata samantam etaṃ mṛdhas saṃprakampante yaṃ sarvato bhayam āgacchati yaivendrasya vimṛdhā tanūs tām eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tayā mṛdho 'pahata ātmano 'dhi |
10.9.d: इन्द्राय सुत्राम्ण एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् अपरुद्धो वापरुरुत्स्यमानो वा । इन्द्रो वै त्रातेन्द्रो ऽपरोद्धा तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनं त्रायते । इन्द्रायांहोमुच एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् आमयावी । अंहसा वा एष गृहीतो य आमयावी । एषेन्द्रस्य भिषज्या तनूर् यांहोमुक् । इन्द्रो ऽंहसो मोक्ता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अंहसो मुञ्चति । इन्द्रायांहोमुच एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् य आत्मना वा गृहैर् वांहूरणम् अवेयात् । अंहसा वा एष गृहीतो य आत्मना वा गृहैर् वांहूरणम् अवैति । इन्द्रो ऽंहसो मोक्ता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति स एनम् अंहसो मुञ्चति । इन्द्रायार्कवते ऽश्वमेधवत एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेत महायज्ञो मोपनमेद् इति । इयं वा अर्को ऽसा अर्कासा अश्वमेध ऐन्द्रो यज्ञस् । अन्तम् एतस्य यज्ञो गच्छति यं यज्ञकामं यज्ञो नोपनमति । एते इन्द्रस्यान्त्ये तन्वौ ये अर्कवती ये एवेन्द्रस्यान्त्ये तन्वौ ताभ्याम् एव यज्ञम् आलभते । उपैनं यज्ञो नमति । इन्द्रायान्वृजव एकादशकपालं निर्वपेत् सजातकामस् । इन्द्रियं वै ज्यैष्ठ्यम् इन्द्रियेणैव सजातान् अन्वृजून् कुरुते । इन्द्राय प्रबभ्रायैकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् भ्रातृव्यवान् वज्रो वै प्रबभ्रः प्रबभ्रेण वा इन्द्रो ऽसुरेभ्यो वज्रं प्राहरत् । वज्रम् एव भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति स्तृणुत एनम् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् इन्द्राय विमृधायैकादशकपालं संग्रामे । ऋद्ध्या एवाग्नेयस् । इन्द्रं वै वृत्रं जघ्निवांसं मृधो ऽसचन्त स एतं वैमृधम् अपश्यत् तेन ता मृधो ऽपाहत वृत्रम् एष जिघांसति यस् संग्रामं जिगीषति यैवेन्द्रस्य विमृधा तनूस् ताम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति तया मृधो ऽपहते हन्ति वृत्रम् । जयति संग्रामम् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् इन्द्राय विमृधायैकादशकपालं यं सर्वतो भयम् आगच्छेत् । ऋद्ध्या एवाग्नेयस् । इन्द्रं वै वृत्रं जघ्निवांसं तं समन्तं मृधस् संप्राकम्पन्त स एतं वैमृधम् अपश्यत् तेन ता मृधो ऽपाहत समन्तम् एतं मृधस् संप्रकम्पन्ते यं सर्वतो भयम् आगच्छति यैवेन्द्रस्य विमृधा तनूस् ताम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति तया मृधो ऽपहत आत्मनो ऽधि ।
10.9.m:
One who is expelled or about to be expelled should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Sutrāman.
Indra is the protector, Indra is the expeller.
He approaches him with his share;
he protects him.
One who is ill should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Aṃhomuc.
He is seized by distress who is ill.
This is Indra's healing body, which is Aṃhomuc.
Indra is the releaser from distress.
He approaches him with his share;
he releases him from distress.
One who through himself or through his house should enter into straits should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Aṃhomuc.
He is seized by distress who through himself or through his house enters into straits.
Indra is the releaser from distress.
He approaches him with his share;
he releases him from distress.
One who desires, "May the great sacrifice come to me," should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Arkavat Aśvamedhavat.
This [earth] is the arka, yonder is the arka, yonder is the Aśvamedha; the sacrifice belongs to Indra.
His sacrifice goes to the end, who, desiring a sacrifice, does not have the sacrifice come to him.
These are Indra's final bodies, which are Arkavatī.
Those which are Indra's final bodies, through them he lays hold of the sacrifice.
The sacrifice comes to him.
One who desires kinsmen should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Anvṛju.
Sensory power is primacy.
By sensory power he makes his kinsmen straightforward.
One who has a rival should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Prababhra.
The thunderbolt is the reddish-brown one.
With the reddish-brown one Indra hurled the thunderbolt at the Asuras.
He hurls the thunderbolt at his rival;
he lays him low.
In battle, one should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni and a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh.
The one to Agni is for prosperity.
When Indra had slain Vṛtra, hostilities attached themselves to him.
He saw this Vaimṛdha [offering];
by it he drove away those hostilities.
He seeks to slay Vṛtra who wishes to win a battle.
That which is Indra's expelling body, he approaches that with its share;
by it he drives away hostilities;
he slays Vṛtra;
he wins the battle.
One whom fear should approach from all sides should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni and a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh.
The one to Agni is for prosperity.
When Indra had slain Vṛtra, hostilities shook him violently all around.
He saw this Vaimṛdha [offering];
by it he drove away those hostilities.
Hostilities shake him violently all around, whom fear approaches from all sides.
That which is Indra's expelling body, he approaches that with its share;
by it he drives away hostilities from himself.

10.10.s: prajāpatir vā indrāya vajraṃ pratyamuñcat | mahānāmnīs tena vyajayata tato vai so 'bhavat so 'bibhed vajro me 'śānto grīvā apidhakṣyatīti tato revatīr niramimīta śāntyai | aindraṃ caruṃ nirvaped rājanyāya bubhūṣate | aindro vai rājanyo devatayā svād evainaṃ yoner janayati bhūtyai bhavaty eva revaty anuvākyā śakvarī yājyā vajro vai revatī vajraś śakvarī vajram eva saṃdadhāti tena vijayate bhavaty eva carur bhavati śāntyai | anuddāhāya | indrāṇyai caruṃ nirvapet senāyām utthitāyāṃ rājño gṛhe senā vā indrāṇī brahmaṇaivaināṃ vittyai saṃśyati balbajā idhme ca barhiṣi cāpibhavanti śakno vā ete jātās | nyāyenaivainām abhinayati yat sā vindeta tato dakṣiṇā samṛddhyai | indrāya cendrāṇyai ca caruṃ nirvapet senāyām utthitāyāṃ rājño gṛhe | eṣā vā indrasya parivṛktī jāyā goṣv evainām adhinayati balbajā idhme ca barhiṣi cāpi bhavanti śakno vā ete jātās | nyāyenaivainām abhinayati yat sā vindeta tato dakṣiṇā samṛddhyai prajāpatir vai devebhyo bhāgadheyāni vyādiśat tad indriyam atyaricyata tad indro 'bravīn mayīdam astv iti tad asminn adadhāt tad enam atyaty evāricyata tad imāṃl lokān ūrdhvam anūdaśrayata tan naikenāpnon na dvitīyena tat tṛtīyenāptvāvārunddha trīn puroḍāśān nirvaped bubhūṣan | traya ime lokās | imān eva lokān āptvaujo vīryam avarunddhe | uttarauttaro jyāyān bhavati | uttarauttaro hy eṣāṃ lokāṇāṃ jyāyān indrāya rājñe prathamam athendrāya svarāje 'thendrāyādhirājāya | etāni vai sarvāṇīndro 'bhavan nod etāny eva sarvāṇi bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān etayā yajate | tisro 'nuvākyās tā yājyās tāsāṃ prathamām anūcya madhyamayā yajati madhyamām anūcyottamayā yajati | uttamām anūcya punaḥ prathamayā yajati | eṣāṃ lokānāṃ saṃtatyai prati prajñātyai sarvā evānuvākyāḥ karoti sarvā yājyās | devāś ca vā asurāś ca saṃyattā āsan | te 'surā bhūyāṃso 'jitamanasa āsan kanīyāṃsaḥ parājitamanastarā iva devās te devā abruvaṃś cikitsata yo no vīryāvattamas tam anusamārabhāmahā iti ta indram abruvaṃs tvaṃ vai no vīryāvattamo 'si tvām anu samārabhāmahā iti so 'bravīt tisro ma imās tanvo vīryāvatīs tā me prīṇītāthaitān abhibhaviṣyāma iti tā vai brūhīty abruvan | iyaṃ vimṛdhety abravīd iyam aṃhomug iyam indriyāvatīti ta indrāya vimṛdhāyaikādaśakapālaṃ niravapann indrāyāṃhomuca ekādaśakapālam indrāyendriyavata ekādaśakapālam | yad indrāya vimṛdhāya mṛdhā vai te 'bhiṣaṇā āsan ye śreyobhir asurair aspardhanta mṛdha eva tenāpāghnata yad indrāyāṃhomuce | aṃhasā vai te gṛhītā āsan | aṃhasa eva tenāmucyanta yad indrāyendriyavate | indriyam eva tenātmann adadhata | etayā yajeta bhrātṛvyavān yo bahubhrātavyas syāt | indrāya vimṛdhāyaikādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped indrāyāṃhomuca ekādaśakapālam indrāyendriyavata ekādaśakapālam | yad indrāya vimṛdhāya mṛdhā vā eṣo 'bhiṣaṇo yaś śreyasā bhrātṛvyeṇa spardhate mṛdha eva tenāpahate yad indrāyāṃhomuce | aṃhasā vā eṣa gṛhīto yo bhrātṛvyavān aṃhasa eva tena mucyate yad indrāyendriyavate | indriyam eva tenātman dhatte trayastriṃśad vai devatās tās taṃ sarvā vīryair anusamārabhanta sa uttamāṃ vijitam asurair vyajayata tato vai so 'bhavat | yat trayastriṃśatkapālāni bhavanti yāvatīr eva devatās tās sarvā vīryair ātmānam anusamārambhayate bhavaty eva saiṣā vijitir nāmeṣṭis | uttamām eva vijitiṃ bhrātṛvyeṇa vijayate ya evaṃ vidvān etayā yajate |
10.10.d: प्रजापतिर् वा इन्द्राय वज्रं प्रत्यमुञ्चत् । महानाम्नीस् तेन व्यजयत ततो वै सो ऽभवत् सो ऽबिभेद् वज्रो मे ऽशान्तो ग्रीवा अपिधक्ष्यतीति ततो रेवतीर् निरमिमीत शान्त्यै । ऐन्द्रं चरुं निर्वपेद् राजन्याय बुभूषते । ऐन्द्रो वै राजन्यो देवतया स्वाद् एवैनं योनेर् जनयति भूत्यै भवत्य् एव रेवत्य् अनुवाक्या शक्वरी याज्या वज्रो वै रेवती वज्रश् शक्वरी वज्रम् एव संदधाति तेन विजयते भवत्य् एव चरुर् भवति शान्त्यै । अनुद्दाहाय । इन्द्राण्यै चरुं निर्वपेत् सेनायाम् उत्थितायां राज्ञो गृहे सेना वा इन्द्राणी ब्रह्मणैवैनां वित्त्यै संश्यति बल्बजा इध्मे च बर्हिषि चापिभवन्ति शक्नो वा एते जातास् । न्यायेनैवैनाम् अभिनयति यत् सा विन्देत ततो दक्षिणा समृद्ध्यै । इन्द्राय चेन्द्राण्यै च चरुं निर्वपेत् सेनायाम् उत्थितायां राज्ञो गृहे । एषा वा इन्द्रस्य परिवृक्ती जाया गोष्व् एवैनाम् अधिनयति बल्बजा इध्मे च बर्हिषि चापि भवन्ति शक्नो वा एते जातास् । न्यायेनैवैनाम् अभिनयति यत् सा विन्देत ततो दक्षिणा समृद्ध्यै प्रजापतिर् वै देवेभ्यो भागधेयानि व्यादिशत् तद् इन्द्रियम् अत्यरिच्यत तद् इन्द्रो ऽब्रवीन् मयीदम् अस्त्व् इति तद् अस्मिन्न् अदधात् तद् एनम् अत्यत्य् एवारिच्यत तद् इमांल् लोकान् ऊर्ध्वम् अनूदश्रयत तन् नैकेनाप्नोन् न द्वितीयेन तत् तृतीयेनाप्त्वावारुन्द्ध त्रीन् पुरोडाशान् निर्वपेद् बुभूषन् । त्रय इमे लोकास् । इमान् एव लोकान् आप्त्वौजो वीर्यम् अवरुन्द्धे । उत्तरौत्तरो ज्यायान् भवति । उत्तरौत्तरो ह्य् एषां लोकाणां ज्यायान् इन्द्राय राज्ञे प्रथमम् अथेन्द्राय स्वराजे ऽथेन्द्रायाधिराजाय । एतानि वै सर्वाणीन्द्रो ऽभवन् नोद् एतान्य् एव सर्वाणि भवति य एवं विद्वान् एतया यजते । तिस्रो ऽनुवाक्यास् ता याज्यास् तासां प्रथमाम् अनूच्य मध्यमया यजति मध्यमाम् अनूच्योत्तमया यजति । उत्तमाम् अनूच्य पुनः प्रथमया यजति । एषां लोकानां संतत्यै प्रति प्रज्ञात्यै सर्वा एवानुवाक्याः करोति सर्वा याज्यास् । देवाश् च वा असुराश् च संयत्ता आसन् । ते ऽसुरा भूयांसो ऽजितमनस आसन् कनीयांसः पराजितमनस्तरा इव देवास् ते देवा अब्रुवंश् चिकित्सत यो नो वीर्यावत्तमस् तम् अनुसमारभामहा इति त इन्द्रम् अब्रुवंस् त्वं वै नो वीर्यावत्तमो ऽसि त्वाम् अनु समारभामहा इति सो ऽब्रवीत् तिस्रो म इमास् तन्वो वीर्यावतीस् ता मे प्रीणीताथैतान् अभिभविष्याम इति ता वै ब्रूहीत्य् अब्रुवन् । इयं विमृधेत्य् अब्रवीद् इयम् अंहोमुग् इयम् इन्द्रियावतीति त इन्द्राय विमृधायैकादशकपालं निरवपन्न् इन्द्रायांहोमुच एकादशकपालम् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवत एकादशकपालम् । यद् इन्द्राय विमृधाय मृधा वै ते ऽभिषणा आसन् ये श्रेयोभिर् असुरैर् अस्पर्धन्त मृध एव तेनापाघ्नत यद् इन्द्रायांहोमुचे । अंहसा वै ते गृहीता आसन् । अंहस एव तेनामुच्यन्त यद् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवते । इन्द्रियम् एव तेनात्मन्न् अदधत । एतया यजेत भ्रातृव्यवान् यो बहुभ्रातव्यस् स्यात् । इन्द्राय विमृधायैकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् इन्द्रायांहोमुच एकादशकपालम् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवत एकादशकपालम् । यद् इन्द्राय विमृधाय मृधा वा एषो ऽभिषणो यश् श्रेयसा भ्रातृव्येण स्पर्धते मृध एव तेनापहते यद् इन्द्रायांहोमुचे । अंहसा वा एष गृहीतो यो भ्रातृव्यवान् अंहस एव तेन मुच्यते यद् इन्द्रायेन्द्रियवते । इन्द्रियम् एव तेनात्मन् धत्ते त्रयस्त्रिंशद् वै देवतास् तास् तं सर्वा वीर्यैर् अनुसमारभन्त स उत्तमां विजितम् असुरैर् व्यजयत ततो वै सो ऽभवत् । यत् त्रयस्त्रिंशत्कपालानि भवन्ति यावतीर् एव देवतास् तास् सर्वा वीर्यैर् आत्मानम् अनुसमारम्भयते भवत्य् एव सैषा विजितिर् नामेष्टिस् । उत्तमाम् एव विजितिं भ्रातृव्येण विजयते य एवं विद्वान् एतया यजते ।
10.10.m:
Prajāpati fastened the thunderbolt onto Indra.
With it he conquered the Mahānāmnī [verses].
Thence indeed he became [great].
He feared: "My thunderbolt, unappeased, will burn up my neck."
Then he fashioned the Revatī [verses]
for appeasement.
One who desires to become [great], being a nobleman, should offer a caru to Indra.
By deity the nobleman is indeed connected with Indra.
From his own womb he produces him
for prosperity;
he indeed becomes [prosperous].
The preparatory verse is a Revatī, the offering verse a Śakvarī.
The thunderbolt is the Revatī, the thunderbolt is the Śakvarī.
He indeed joins the thunderbolt [together];
by it he conquers;
he indeed becomes [prosperous].
It is a caru,
for appeasement,
not to cause burning.
One should offer a caru to Indrāṇī when an army has arisen in the king's house.
The army is Indrāṇī.
Through sacred lore he sharpens her for acquisition.
Balbaja grass is mixed into the firewood and the barhis;
for these are born from dung.
In accordance with proper order he leads her.
Whatever she obtains, from that is the sacrificial gift,
for success.
And one should offer a caru to Indra and Indrāṇī when an army has arisen in the king's house.
She is Indra's discarded wife;
he places her over cattle.
Balbaja grass is also mixed into the firewood and the barhis;
for these are born from dung.
In accordance with proper order he leads her.
Whatever she obtains, from that is the sacrificial gift,
for success.
Prajāpati allotted the portions to the gods; then the sensory power was left over.
Indra said to it: "Let this be in me."
He placed that in him.
It overflowed beyond him.
It arose upwards along these worlds.
He did not reach it with one, nor with a second; having reached it with the third, he attained it.
One who desires to become [great] should offer three cakes.
Three are these worlds.
Having reached these very worlds, he secures vigor and heroic power.
Each succeeding one is greater;
for each succeeding one of these worlds is greater:
to Indra the king first, then to Indra the self-ruler, then to Indra the overlord.
Indra indeed became all these, not otherwise;
all these indeed becomes he who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this [offering].
There are three preparatory verses; they are the offering verses.
Having recited the first of them, he sacrifices with the middle one;
having recited the middle one, he sacrifices with the highest;
having recited the highest, he sacrifices again with the first,
for the continuity of these worlds,
for recognition.
All he makes preparatory verses, all offering verses.
The gods and the Asuras were in conflict.
Those Asuras were more numerous and unconquered in mind; the gods were fewer and, as it were, more defeated in mind.
Those gods said: "Consider: let us take hold of him among us who is most full of heroic power."
They said to Indra: "You indeed are the most full of heroic power among us; let us take hold of you."
He said: "Three are these bodies of mine full of heroic power; please these for me, and then we will overcome them."
"Tell them indeed!" they said.
"This one is Vimṛdh," he said, "this one Aṃhomuc, this one Indriyavat."
They offered a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Aṃhomuc, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Indriyavat.
In that [it is] to Indra Vimṛdh:
they who contended with the Asuras, who were superior, had foes confronting them;
they struck away foes by that.
In that [it is] to Indra Aṃhomuc:
they were seized by distress;
they were freed from distress by that.
In that [it is] to Indra Indriyavat:
they placed sensory power in themselves by that.
One who has rivals, who has many rivals, should sacrifice with this [offering]:
he should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Aṃhomuc, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Indriyavat.
In that [it is] to Indra Vimṛdh:
he who contends with a rival who is superior has a foe confronting him;
he strikes away foes by that.
In that [it is] to Indra Aṃhomuc:
he who has rivals is seized by distress;
he is freed from distress by that.
In that [it is] to Indra Indriyavat:
he places sensory power in himself by that.
Thirty-three indeed are the deities;
they all took hold of him with heroic powers.
He won the highest victory over the Asuras;
thence indeed he became [great].
In that there are thirty-three potsherds:
as many as the deities are, all of them he causes to take hold of himself with heroic powers;
he indeed becomes [prosperous].
This is the sacrifice named Vijiti ("Conquest").
He wins the highest victory over his rival who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this [offering].

10.11.s: prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smād apākrāman | teṣāṃ bṛhaspatiś ca padenānvaitām | te yatrāvasaṃs tad garmutaṃ śakno jātām avindatām | ām ācchidyāharatām | taṃ bṛhaspatir abravīd anayā tvā yājayāny upa vai tvaite paśavaḥ punar naṃsyantīti sa prājāpatyaṃ caruṃ niravapad gārmutam apsu tato vai taṃ paśavaḥ punar upānaman prājāpatyaṃ caruṃ nirvaped gārmutam apsu paśukāmas | apakrāntā vā etasmāt paśavo yo 'paśuḥ prajāpatiḥ paśūnāṃ pradātā tam eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati so 'smai paśūn punar upāvartayati gomūtrasyāpi syāt sayonitvāya prajāpatiḥ paśūn sṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ pūṣaṇam adhipām akarot te 'smād apākrāman | teṣāṃ pūṣā padenānvait te yatrāvasaṃs tad garmutam | śakno jātām avindat tām ācchidyāharat tayā prajāpatim abravīd anayā mā pratiṣṭhasvopa vai tvaite paśavaḥ punar naṃsyantīti tat somo 'bhyārtīyata | mama vā etad yad akṛṣṭapacyam iti sa saumāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ niravapad gārmutam apsu tato vai taṃ paśavaḥ punar upānaman saumāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvaped gārmutam apsu prajākāmo vā paśukāmo vā somo vai retodhāḥ pūṣā prajanayitā soma evāsmai reto dadhāti pūṣā prajanayati vindate prajā vā paśūn vā yatarasmai kāmāya nirvapati gomūtrasyāpi syāt sayonitvāya mārutaṃ praiyaṅgavaṃ caruṃ nirvapet pṛśnyā dugdhe sajātakāmaḥ pṛśnyā vai maruto jātā vāco vāsyā vā pṛthivyā mārutās sajātās | etan marutāṃ svaṃ payo yat priyaṅgavas svenaivainān payasācchaiti yathā vatsa ūdho 'bhyāyacchaty evam enaṃ sajātā abhyāyacchanti | priyavaty anuvākyā śrīvatī yājyā yat priyavatī priyam evainaṃ sajātānāṃ karoti yac chrīvatī śriyam evainaṃ gamayati dvipadānuvākyā catuṣpadā yājyā dvipadaś caiva catuṣpadaś ca paśūn avarunddhe | aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mārutaṃ praiyaṅgavaṃ carum | taṃ paścā śṛtaṃ kuryur yasmāt kṣatriyād viḍ abhyardhaś caret kṣatraṃ vā indro viṇ marutaḥ kṣatrāyaiva viśam anuniyunakti tam anūcyamāne paścāt prāñcam udāharanti viśam evāsmai paścād upadadhāti | asaṃsargāya mārutaṃ saptakapālaṃ nirvaped aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ yaḥ kāmayeta viśe ca kṣatrāya ca samadaṃ kuryām iti kṣatraṃ vā indro viṇ marutas | bhāgadheya evaibhyas samadaṃ karoti mārutasya mārutīm anūcyaindryā yajet | aindrasyaindrīm anūcya mārutyā yajet kṣatram eva viśaḥ parihāyādatte viṭ kṣatrasya te anyānyāṃ nirṇayatas | ubhayataḥ puroḍāśasyāvadyed yatarān kāmayeta parājayerann iti | ubhayata eva viśam upadīpayati tājak parājayante | etām eva nirvaped yadā kāmayeta kalperann iti tasyāḥ prasṛtiṃ yajet | bhāgadheyenaivainān kalpayati mārutaṃ saptakapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kṣatriyo viśo jyānyā bibhīyāt | brāhmaṇo vā viḍ vai marutas | bhāgadheyenaivaināñ chamayati | agastyasyaitat sūktaṃ kayāśubhīyam | tasya sāmidhenīṣv apy anubrūyāt tasya yājyānuvākye syātām agastyo vai marudbhyaś śatam ukṣṇaḥ pṛśnīn praukṣat tān indrāyālabhata taṃ marutaḥ kruddhā vajram udyatyābhyapatan sa etat sūktam apaśyat tenainān aśamayat | yad etad anūcyate śāntyai |
10.11.d: प्रजापतिः पशून् असृजत ते ऽस्माद् अपाक्रामन् । तेषां बृहस्पतिश् च पदेनान्वैताम् । ते यत्रावसंस् तद् गर्मुतं शक्नो जाताम् अविन्दताम् । आम् आच्छिद्याहरताम् । तं बृहस्पतिर् अब्रवीद् अनया त्वा याजयान्य् उप वै त्वैते पशवः पुनर् नंस्यन्तीति स प्राजापत्यं चरुं निरवपद् गार्मुतम् अप्सु ततो वै तं पशवः पुनर् उपानमन् प्राजापत्यं चरुं निर्वपेद् गार्मुतम् अप्सु पशुकामस् । अपक्रान्ता वा एतस्मात् पशवो यो ऽपशुः प्रजापतिः पशूनां प्रदाता तम् एव भागधेयेनोपधावति सो ऽस्मै पशून् पुनर् उपावर्तयति गोमूत्रस्यापि स्यात् सयोनित्वाय प्रजापतिः पशून् सृष्ट्वा तेषां पूषणम् अधिपाम् अकरोत् ते ऽस्माद् अपाक्रामन् । तेषां पूषा पदेनान्वैत् ते यत्रावसंस् तद् गर्मुतम् । शक्नो जाताम् अविन्दत् ताम् आच्छिद्याहरत् तया प्रजापतिम् अब्रवीद् अनया मा प्रतिष्ठस्वोप वै त्वैते पशवः पुनर् नंस्यन्तीति तत् सोमो ऽभ्यार्तीयत । मम वा एतद् यद् अकृष्टपच्यम् इति स सौमापौष्णं चरुं निरवपद् गार्मुतम् अप्सु ततो वै तं पशवः पुनर् उपानमन् सौमापौष्णं चरुं निर्वपेद् गार्मुतम् अप्सु प्रजाकामो वा पशुकामो वा सोमो वै रेतोधाः पूषा प्रजनयिता सोम एवास्मै रेतो दधाति पूषा प्रजनयति विन्दते प्रजा वा पशून् वा यतरस्मै कामाय निर्वपति गोमूत्रस्यापि स्यात् सयोनित्वाय मारुतं प्रैयङ्गवं चरुं निर्वपेत् पृश्न्या दुग्धे सजातकामः पृश्न्या वै मरुतो जाता वाचो वास्या वा पृथिव्या मारुतास् सजातास् । एतन् मरुतां स्वं पयो यत् प्रियङ्गवस् स्वेनैवैनान् पयसाच्छैति यथा वत्स ऊधो ऽभ्यायच्छत्य् एवम् एनं सजाता अभ्यायच्छन्ति । प्रियवत्य् अनुवाक्या श्रीवती याज्या यत् प्रियवती प्रियम् एवैनं सजातानां करोति यच् छ्रीवती श्रियम् एवैनं गमयति द्विपदानुवाक्या चतुष्पदा याज्या द्विपदश् चैव चतुष्पदश् च पशून् अवरुन्द्धे । ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेन् मारुतं प्रैयङ्गवं चरुम् । तं पश्चा शृतं कुर्युर् यस्मात् क्षत्रियाद् विड् अभ्यर्धश् चरेत् क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो विण् मरुतः क्षत्रायैव विशम् अनुनियुनक्ति तम् अनूच्यमाने पश्चात् प्राञ्चम् उदाहरन्ति विशम् एवास्मै पश्चाद् उपदधाति । असंसर्गाय मारुतं सप्तकपालं निर्वपेद् ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं यः कामयेत विशे च क्षत्राय च समदं कुर्याम् इति क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो विण् मरुतस् । भागधेय एवैभ्यस् समदं करोति मारुतस्य मारुतीम् अनूच्यैन्द्र्या यजेत् । ऐन्द्रस्यैन्द्रीम् अनूच्य मारुत्या यजेत् क्षत्रम् एव विशः परिहायादत्ते विट् क्षत्रस्य ते अन्यान्यां निर्णयतस् । उभयतः पुरोडाशस्यावद्येद् यतरान् कामयेत पराजयेरन्न् इति । उभयत एव विशम् उपदीपयति ताजक् पराजयन्ते । एताम् एव निर्वपेद् यदा कामयेत कल्पेरन्न् इति तस्याः प्रसृतिं यजेत् । भागधेयेनैवैनान् कल्पयति मारुतं सप्तकपालं निर्वपेद् यः क्षत्रियो विशो ज्यान्या बिभीयात् । ब्राह्मणो वा विड् वै मरुतस् । भागधेयेनैवैनाञ् छमयति । अगस्त्यस्यैतत् सूक्तं कयाशुभीयम् । तस्य सामिधेनीष्व् अप्य् अनुब्रूयात् तस्य याज्यानुवाक्ये स्याताम् अगस्त्यो वै मरुद्भ्यश् शतम् उक्ष्णः पृश्नीन् प्रौक्षत् तान् इन्द्रायालभत तं मरुतः क्रुद्धा वज्रम् उद्यत्याभ्यपतन् स एतत् सूक्तम् अपश्यत् तेनैनान् अशमयत् । यद् एतद् अनूच्यते शान्त्यै ।
10.11.m:
Prajāpati created domestic animals.
They departed from him.
Bṛhaspati and [Prajāpati] followed them by their track.
Where they dwelt, there they found garmut grass growing from cow-dung.
They broke off and brought it.
Bṛhaspati said to him: "Let me sacrifice with this for you; these domestic animals will bow down to you again."
He offered a caru of garmut to Prajāpati in water; then indeed the domestic animals bowed down to him again.
One who desires domestic animals should offer a caru of garmut to Prajāpati in water.
From him the domestic animals have departed who has no domestic animals.
Prajāpati is the bestower of domestic animals.
He approaches him with his share;
he turns the domestic animals back to him.
There should also be cow's urine,
for identity of origin.
Having created domestic animals, Prajāpati made Pūṣan their overlord.
They departed from him.
Pūṣan followed them by their track.
Where they dwelt, there [he found] garmut.
He found it growing from cow-dung.
He broke off and brought it.
With it he said to Prajāpati: "Establish yourself with this; these domestic animals will bow down to you again."
Soma was distressed at that:
"This is mine, which ripens without cultivation."
He offered a caru of garmut to Soma and Pūṣan in water.
Then indeed the domestic animals bowed down to him again.
One who desires offspring or desires domestic animals should offer a caru of garmut to Soma and Pūṣan in water.
Soma is the placer of semen;
Pūṣan is the begetter.
Soma places semen in him;
Pūṣan begets.
He obtains offspring or domestic animals, whichever desire he offers for.
There should also be cow's urine,
for identity of origin.
One who desires relatives should offer a caru of priyaṅgu to the Maruts in the milk of a speckled cow.
From a speckled cow the Maruts were born, or from speech, or from this
earth; the Maruts are relatives.
This is the Maruts' own milk, which is priyaṅgu.
He approaches them with their own milk.
As a calf stretches towards the udder, so his relatives stretch towards him.
The preparatory verse contains [the word] "dear" (priyávat); the offering verse contains [the word] "splendor" (śrī́vat).
Because it contains "dear",
he makes him dear to his relatives.
Because it contains "splendor",
he causes him to attain splendor.
The preparatory verse has two feet; the offering verse has four feet.
He wins two-footed and four-footed domestic animals.
He should offer [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra, [and] a caru of priyaṅgu to the Maruts.
They should cook it behind, for that nobleman from whom the people wander apart.
Indra is the nobility; the Maruts are the people.
He assigns the people to the nobility.
While it is being recited, they bring it forward from behind.
He places the people behind him,
so that they do not mingle.
He should offer [a cake] on seven potsherds to the Maruts [and a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra, who should desire: "May I create strife between the people and the nobility."
Indra is the nobility; the Maruts are the people.
He creates strife for them in their share.
Having recited the preparatory verse of the Maruts for that of the Maruts, he should sacrifice with that of Indra.
Having recited the preparatory verse of Indra for that of Indra, he should sacrifice with that of the Maruts.
The nobility takes away, having encircled the people;
the people [encircles] the nobility.
They lead each other away.
He should cut off from both sides of the sacrificial cake, whichever of the two he should desire: "May they be defeated."
He inflames the people from both sides;
they are swiftly defeated.
He should offer this very [sacrifice] when he should desire: "May they be harmonized."
He should sacrifice a handful of it.
He harmonizes them with their share.
That nobleman should offer [a cake] on seven potsherds to the Maruts who should fear oppression by the people.
The Maruts are the Brahmin or the people.
He appeases them with their share.
This is Agastya's hymn, the Kayāśubhīya.
He should also recite it among the kindling verses;
its [verses] should be the preparatory and offering verses.
Agastya sprinkled a hundred speckled oxen for the Maruts;
he seized them for Indra.
Angry, having raised the thunderbolt, the Maruts flew at him.
He saw this hymn;
with it he appeased them.
In that this is recited,
[it is] for appeasement.

10.12.s: asmai te pratiharyate jātavedo vicarṣaṇe | agne janāmi suṣṭutim | yasmai tvaṃ sukṛte jātaveda u lokam agne kṛṇavas syonam | aśvinaṃ sa putriṇaṃ vīravantaṃ gomantaṃ rayiṃ naśate svasti | ya imā viśvā jātāny āśrāvayati ślokena | pra ca suvāti savitā | viśvā rūpāṇi | vāyur agregā yajñaprīs sākaṃ gan manasā yajñam | śivo niyudbhiś śivābhiḥ | pra yābhir yāsi dāśvāṃsam acchā niyudbhir vāya iṣṭaye duroṇe | ni no rayiṃ subhojasaṃ yuvasva ni vīraṃ gavyam aśvyaṃ ca rādhaḥ | baḍ itthā parvatānāṃ khidraṃ bibharṣi pṛthivi | pra yā bhūmiṃ pravatvati mahnā jinoṣi mahini | dṛḍhā cid yā vanaspatīn kṣmayā dardharṣy ojasā | yat te abhrasya vidyuto divo varṣanti vṛṣṭayaḥ | ā no agne rayiṃ bhara satrāsāhaṃ vareṇyam | viśvāsu pṛtsu duṣṭaram | gomāṃ agne | mademade hi no dadir yūthā gavām ṛjukratuḥ | saṃ gṛbhāya purū śatobhayāhastyā vasu śiśīhi rāya ābhara | śiprin vājānāṃ pate śacīvas tava daṃsanā | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha | revatīr naḥ pra sasāhiṣe | saṃjñānaṃ no divā paśos saṃjñānaṃ naktam arvataḥ | saṃjñānaṃ nas svebhyas saṃjñānam araṇebhyas saṃjñānam aśvinā yuvam ihāsmāsu niyacchatam | sam indra rāyā sam iṣā rabhemahi saṃ vājebhiḥ puruścandrair abhidyubhiḥ | saṃ devyā pramatyā vīraśuṣmayā goagrayāśvāvatyā rabhemahi | indravāyū susaṃdṛśā suhaveha havāmahe | yathā nas sarva ij janas saṃgame sumanā asat | agniḥ prathamo vasubhir no avyāt somo rudrair abhirakṣatu tmanā | indro marudbhir ṛtuthā kṛṇotv ādityair no varuṇaś śarma yaṃsat | sam agnir vasubhir no avyāt saṃ somo rudriyābhis tanūbhiḥ | sam indro rātahavyo marudbhis sam ādityair varuṇo viśvavedāḥ | samānā va ākūtāni samānā hṛdayāni vaḥ | samānam astu vo mano yathā vas susahāsati | saṃ vo manāṃsi saṃ vratā sam u cittāny ākaram | amī ye vivratās sthana tān vas saṃnamayāmasi | yathādityam ādityā āpyāyayanti yathākṣitim akṣitayo madanti | evā mām indro varuṇo bṛhaspatir āpyāyayantu bhuvanasya gopāḥ | navonavo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ ketur uṣasām ety agram | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vidadhāty āyan pra candramās tirate dīrgham āyuḥ |
10.12.d: अस्मै ते प्रतिहर्यते जातवेदो विचर्षणे । अग्ने जनामि सुष्टुतिम् । यस्मै त्वं सुकृते जातवेद उ लोकम् अग्ने कृणवस् स्योनम् । अश्विनं स पुत्रिणं वीरवन्तं गोमन्तं रयिं नशते स्वस्ति । य इमा विश्वा जातान्य् आश्रावयति श्लोकेन । प्र च सुवाति सविता । विश्वा रूपाणि । वायुर् अग्रेगा यज्ञप्रीस् साकं गन् मनसा यज्ञम् । शिवो नियुद्भिश् शिवाभिः । प्र याभिर् यासि दाश्वांसम् अच्छा नियुद्भिर् वाय इष्टये दुरोणे । नि नो रयिं सुभोजसं युवस्व नि वीरं गव्यम् अश्व्यं च राधः । बड् इत्था पर्वतानां खिद्रं बिभर्षि पृथिवि । प्र या भूमिं प्रवत्वति मह्ना जिनोषि महिनि । दृढा चिद् या वनस्पतीन् क्ष्मया दर्धर्ष्य् ओजसा । यत् ते अभ्रस्य विद्युतो दिवो वर्षन्ति वृष्टयः । आ नो अग्ने रयिं भर सत्रासाहं वरेण्यम् । विश्वासु पृत्सु दुष्टरम् । गोमां अग्ने । मदेमदे हि नो ददिर् यूथा गवाम् ऋजुक्रतुः । सं गृभाय पुरू शतोभयाहस्त्या वसु शिशीहि राय आभर । शिप्रिन् वाजानां पते शचीवस् तव दंसना । आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्व् अश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ । रेवतीर् नः प्र ससाहिषे । संज्ञानं नो दिवा पशोस् संज्ञानं नक्तम् अर्वतः । संज्ञानं नस् स्वेभ्यस् संज्ञानम् अरणेभ्यस् संज्ञानम् अश्विना युवम् इहास्मासु नियच्छतम् । सम् इन्द्र राया सम् इषा रभेमहि सं वाजेभिः पुरुश्चन्द्रैर् अभिद्युभिः । सं देव्या प्रमत्या वीरशुष्मया गोअग्रयाश्वावत्या रभेमहि । इन्द्रवायू सुसंदृशा सुहवेह हवामहे । यथा नस् सर्व इज् जनस् संगमे सुमना असत् । अग्निः प्रथमो वसुभिर् नो अव्यात् सोमो रुद्रैर् अभिरक्षतु त्मना । इन्द्रो मरुद्भिर् ऋतुथा कृणोत्व् आदित्यैर् नो वरुणश् शर्म यंसत् । सम् अग्निर् वसुभिर् नो अव्यात् सं सोमो रुद्रियाभिस् तनूभिः । सम् इन्द्रो रातहव्यो मरुद्भिस् सम् आदित्यैर् वरुणो विश्ववेदाः । समाना व आकूतानि समाना हृदयानि वः । समानम् अस्तु वो मनो यथा वस् सुसहासति । सं वो मनांसि सं व्रता सम् उ चित्तान्य् आकरम् । अमी ये विव्रतास् स्थन तान् वस् संनमयामसि । यथादित्यम् आदित्या आप्याययन्ति यथाक्षितिम् अक्षितयो मदन्ति । एवा माम् इन्द्रो वरुणो बृहस्पतिर् आप्याययन्तु भुवनस्य गोपाः । नवोनवो भवति जायमानो ऽह्नां केतुर् उषसाम् एत्य् अग्रम् । भागं देवेभ्यो विदधात्य् आयन् प्र चन्द्रमास् तिरते दीर्घम् आयुः ।
10.12.m:
For you who take pleasure in this, O active Jātavedas, / I produce a song of praise, O Agni!
For whichever virtuous man you make a pleasant place, O Agni Jātavedas, / he, possessing horses, sons, heroes, and cattle, attains wealth safely.
He who makes all these creatures hear with his call, / and impels them forward—Savitṛ.
All forms […].
Vāyu, going in front, satisfying the sacrifice, went together with the mind to the sacrifice, / propitious with his propitious teams of horses.
With those teams of horses with which you go to the worshipper, O Vāyu, for the sacrifice in his dwelling, / bring wealth affording good enjoyment, bring a hero, cattle, and horses as wealth.
Truly indeed, O Earth, you bear the weight of the mountains, / you who, possessing slopes, exhilarate the ground with your might, O mighty one!
You who, firm indeed, uphold the trees upon the earth by your power,
when the lightnings of your cloud rain showers from the sky.
Bring us wealth, O Agni, completely overcoming, excellent, / invincible in all battles.
Possessed of cattle, O Agni […].
For at every intoxicating drink he is the giver to us of herds of cattle, of straight intention; / seize much wealth with both hands by hundreds; / sharpen, bring wealth!
O broad-jawed one, lord of prizes, powerful one, such are your wondrous deeds; / make known to us, O Indra, among the cattle, the splendid horses, / the thousands, O bountiful one!
Our Revatī verses […].
You have completely conquered […].
Agreement for us by day with the cattle, agreement by night with the courser, / agreement for us with our own, agreement with strangers; / do both of you, O Aśvins, establish agreement here among us!
May we grasp wealth together, O Indra, nourishment together, prizes together—resplendent, shining afar; / may we grasp together divine foresight, fierce with heroes, excelling in cattle, possessed of horses!
We invoke Indra and Vāyu of fair appearance, easy to invoke here, / so that all our people in the assembly may be of good mind.
May Agni with the Vasus protect us first; may Soma with the Rudras guard us himself; / may Indra with the Maruts act in season; may Varuṇa with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Agni with the Vasus protect us, Soma with his Rudrian bodies, / Indra, receiver of offerings, with the Maruts, Varuṇa who knows all with the Ādityas.
United be your intentions, united your hearts; / united be your mind, so that it may go well together for you.
Together I bring your minds, together your vows, and together your thoughts; / those of you who have contrary vows, them we cause to bend toward you.
Just as the Ādityas cause the sun to swell, just as the imperishable ones rejoice in imperishability, / even so let Indra, Varuṇa, and Bṛhaspati, the guardians of the world, cause me to swell.
Becoming new and new, he is born, the banner of days, he goes before the dawns; / arriving, he distributes their share to the gods; the moon extends long life.

10.13.s: pra yo jajñe vidvāṃ asya bandhuṃ viśvā devānāṃ janimā vivakti | brahma brahmaṇa ujjabhāra madhyān nīcād uccā svadhayābhi pratasthau | mahān mahī askabhāyad vi jāto dyāṃ dvitā pārthivaṃ ca rajaḥ | sa budhnād āṣṭa januṣābhy agraṃ bṛhaspatir devatā tasya samrāṭ | gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ havāmahe kaviṃ kavīnām upamaśravastamam | jyeṣṭharājaṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmaṇaspata ā naś śṛṇvann ūtibhis sīda sādanam | sa suṣṭubhā sa ṛkvatā gaṇena valaṃ ruroja phaligaṃ raveṇa | bṛhaspatir usriyā havyasūdaḥ kanikradad vāvaśatīr udājat | agnir ukthe purohito grāvāṇo barhir adhvare | ṛcā yāmi maruto brahmaṇaspatiṃ devāṃ avo vareṇyam | uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate devayantas tvemahe | upa prayantu marutas sudānava indra prāśūr bhavā sacā | āryamā yātu vṛṣabhas tuviṣmān yantā vasūni vidhate tanūpāḥ | sahasrākṣo gotrabhid vajrabāhur asmāsu devo draviṇaṃ dadhātu | ye te aryaman bahavo devayānāḥ panthāno rājan diva ācaranti | tebhir no adya pathibhis sugebhī rakṣā ca no adhi ca brūhi deva | asme indrābṛhaspatī rayiṃ dhattaṃ śatagvinam | aśvāvantaṃ sahasriṇam | bṛhaspatir naḥ paripātu paścād utottarasmād adharād aghāyoḥ | indraḥ purastād uta madhyato nas sakhā sakhibhyo varivaḥ kṛṇotu | hiraṇyagarbhas | yaḥ prāṇatas | ud u tyam | citraṃ devānām | taraṇir viśvadarśato jyotiṣkṛd asi sūrya | viśvam ābhāsi rocanam | divo rukma urucakṣā udeti dūrearthas taraṇir bhrājamānaḥ | nūnaṃ janās sūryeṇa prasūtā ayann arthāni kṛṇavann apāṃsi | iti śrīyajuṣi carakaśākhāyām iṭhimikāyām āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ nāma daśamaṃ sthānakaṃ saṃpūrṇam |
10.13.d: प्र यो जज्ञे विद्वां अस्य बन्धुं विश्वा देवानां जनिमा विवक्ति । ब्रह्म ब्रह्मण उज्जभार मध्यान् नीचाद् उच्चा स्वधयाभि प्रतस्थौ । महान् मही अस्कभायद् वि जातो द्यां द्विता पार्थिवं च रजः । स बुध्नाद् आष्ट जनुषाभ्य् अग्रं बृहस्पतिर् देवता तस्य सम्राट् । गणानां त्वा गणपतिं हवामहे कविं कवीनाम् उपमश्रवस्तमम् । ज्येष्ठराजं ब्रह्मणां ब्रह्मणस्पत आ नश् शृण्वन्न् ऊतिभिस् सीद सादनम् । स सुष्टुभा स ऋक्वता गणेन वलं रुरोज फलिगं रवेण । बृहस्पतिर् उस्रिया हव्यसूदः कनिक्रदद् वावशतीर् उदाजत् । अग्निर् उक्थे पुरोहितो ग्रावाणो बर्हिर् अध्वरे । ऋचा यामि मरुतो ब्रह्मणस्पतिं देवां अवो वरेण्यम् । उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पते देवयन्तस् त्वेमहे । उप प्रयन्तु मरुतस् सुदानव इन्द्र प्राशूर् भवा सचा । आर्यमा यातु वृषभस् तुविष्मान् यन्ता वसूनि विधते तनूपाः । सहस्राक्षो गोत्रभिद् वज्रबाहुर् अस्मासु देवो द्रविणं दधातु । ये ते अर्यमन् बहवो देवयानाः पन्थानो राजन् दिव आचरन्ति । तेभिर् नो अद्य पथिभिस् सुगेभी रक्षा च नो अधि च ब्रूहि देव । अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती रयिं धत्तं शतग्विनम् । अश्वावन्तं सहस्रिणम् । बृहस्पतिर् नः परिपातु पश्चाद् उतोत्तरस्माद् अधराद् अघायोः । इन्द्रः पुरस्ताद् उत मध्यतो नस् सखा सखिभ्यो वरिवः कृणोतु । हिरण्यगर्भस् । यः प्राणतस् । उद् उ त्यम् । चित्रं देवानाम् । तरणिर् विश्वदर्शतो ज्योतिष्कृद् असि सूर्य । विश्वम् आभासि रोचनम् । दिवो रुक्म उरुचक्षा उदेति दूरेअर्थस् तरणिर् भ्राजमानः । नूनं जनास् सूर्येण प्रसूता अयन्न् अर्थानि कृणवन्न् अपांसि । इति श्रीयजुषि चरकशाखायाम् इठिमिकायाम् आग्नावैष्णवं नाम दशमं स्थानकं संपूर्णम् ।
10.13.m:
He who was born as the wise one, knowing his kinship, proclaims all the births of the gods; / he drew up the sacred word from the midst of the Brahman; from below, upward he stood forth according to his nature.
Being great, when born he propped apart the great sky and double earthly realm; / from the bottom he reached to the summit by his birth; Bṛhaspati is the sovereign deity of it.
We invoke you, the leader of hosts among the hosts, the poet among poets, of highest renown, / the eldest king among sacred words, O Brahmaṇaspati; listening to us, sit upon our seat with aids!
With his well-praising, singing host, with a roar he shattered Vala the rock-cave; / roaring, Bṛhaspati drove up the milch cows that sweeten the offering, lowing aloud.
Agni is the domestic priest at the hymn, the pressing-stones, the sacrificial grass at the rite; / with a verse I seek the Maruts, Brahmaṇaspati, the gods' choice aid.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati; desiring the gods, we approach you; / may the bounteous Maruts advance; O Indra, be swift in company [with us]!
May Aryaman come, the mighty bull, the restrainer, who guards the body, granting wealth to the worshipper; / may the thousand-eyed, pen-splitting, thunderbolt-armed god establish wealth in us.
Those paths of yours, O Aryaman, that are many, god-traveled, that proceed from heaven, O king, / by those easy paths protect us today, and speak favorably for us, O god!
Grant us, O Indra and Bṛhaspati, wealth consisting of hundreds of cattle, / possessed of horses, consisting of thousands!
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, also from above, from below, from the malicious one; / may Indra from in front and from our midst, a friend to friends, make wide space!
The golden embryo […]; / he who by his breath […]; / up that […]; / wonderful of the gods […].
Crossing over, visible to all, maker of light are you, O Sūrya; / you illumine the entire bright realm!
The ornament of heaven, wide-seeing, rises, aiming far, crossing over, resplendent; / now impelled by the sun, men go to their aims and perform their works.
Thus ends the tenth sthānaka named Āgnāvaiṣṇava in the Iṭhimikā of the Caraka recension in the auspicious Yajurveda.

11.1.s: mārutaṃ caruṃ nirvapet tasyaikaviṃśatinirbādho harito rukmo 'pidhānas syāt tasyāpagrāham avadyed yat kṣatriyaṃ viṇ nirbādhe kurvīta viḍ vai marutas | bhāgadheyenaivaināñ chamayati | ekaviṃśatinirbādho bhavati | ekaviṃśatir vai mārutā gaṇās | yad ekaviṃśatinirbādhas | nirbādhair evaiṣāṃ nirbādhān vṛṅkte | aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped vaiśvadevaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ sajātakāmaḥ kṣatraṃ vā indro vaiśvadevīr imāḥ prajāḥ kṣatrāyaiva viśam anuniyunakti | aindrasyāvadāyātha vaiśvadevasyobhe avadāne avadyed athaindrasya kṣatraṃ vā indro vaiśvadevīr imāḥ prajāḥ kṣatreṇaiva viśam ubhayataḥ parigṛhṇāti | aindrī vaiśvadevavarṇe yājyānuvākye bhavatas samṛddhyai | upacāyyapṛḍaṃ hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā sajātān evāsmā upadadhāti tad etad anuvartma nāma havis sajātān evāsmā anuvartmanaḥ karoti saumyaṃ śyāmākaṃ caruṃ nirvapet somavāmī | indro vai tvaṣṭus somam anupahūto 'pibat sa viṣvak somapīthena vyārdhyata tasmāt somo nānupahūtena pātavai somapīthena vyardhuko bhavati sa yat parāvamīt te śyāmākās | eṣa vāva sa somapītho yac chyāmākas samakṣam eva somapītham avarunddhe saumendraḥ kāryas | indriyeṇa vā eṣa somapīthena vyṛdhyate yas somaṃ vamiti saumyo brāhmaṇo devatayā | indriyam asya somapītho yat saumendras | indriyeṇaivainaṃ sompīthena samardhayati | adhṛto vā etasmin somapītho yas somaṃ vamiti taṇḍulān ucchiṃṣet tān kvathati pratyāvapet somapītham evāsmin dādhāra | agnaye jyotiṣmate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet sauryaṃ carum agnaye jyotiṣmata upariṣṭād aṣṭākapālaṃ cakṣuṣkāmas | agner vai manuṣyā naktaṃ cakṣuṣā paśyanti sūryasya divā tau cakṣuṣaḥ pradātārau tā eva bhāgadheyenopadhāvati tā asmai cakṣuḥ prayacchatas | yat samānī devatā dvedhā kriyate tasmāt samānaṃ sac cakṣur dvedhā tasmāt samānī yājyānuvākye bhavatas sauryasya madhyato 'vadyati | idam eva tena karoti yad idam antarā cakṣuṣī cakṣuṣor vyāvṛttyai trīn piṇḍān prayacchati | ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam ayukta sapta śundhyuvas sapta tvā harito ratha iti cakṣur evāsmai tat prayacchati yad eva tasya tat saiṣā rājanī nāmeṣṭis | etayā ha vai rajanaṃ kauṇeyaṃ kratujijjānakiś cakṣuṣkāmaṃ yājayāṃcakāra tayaitayā cakṣuṣkāma eva yajeta | āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ bārhaspatyam aṣṭākapālaṃ bubhūṣan | indro vā adhṛtaś śithila ivāmanyata so 'gnau caiva bṛhaspatau cānāthata tam etayeṣṭyāyājayatām | yad āgneyas teja evāsmiṃs tena purastād adhattām | yad aindras | indriyam evāsmiṃs tena madhyato 'dhattām | yad bārhaspatyas | upariṣṭād evāsmiṃs tena brahmavarcasam adhattām | tato vai so 'bhavat | etayā yajeta bubhūṣan yad āgneyas tejo vā agnis teja eva tena purastād dhatte yad aindras | indriyaṃ vā indras | indriyam eva tena madhyato dhatte yad bārhaspatyas | brahma vai bṛhaspatis | upariṣṭād eva tena brahmavarcasaṃ dhatte bhavaty eva | aindra itarayor nābhī samādadhāti | indriyam evāsmin madhyatas samādadhāti | aindro madhye bhavaty abhita itarau tejo vā agnir indriyam indro brahma bṛhaspatis tejasā caiva brahmavarcasena cendriyam ubhayata ātman parigṛhṇāti trivatīr yājyānuvākyā bhavanti samṛddhyai tad etat tridhātu nāma havis trīṇi hi sa tena vīryāṇy adhatta |
11.1.d: मारुतं चरुं निर्वपेत् तस्यैकविंशतिनिर्बाधो हरितो रुक्मो ऽपिधानस् स्यात् तस्यापग्राहम् अवद्येद् यत् क्षत्रियं विण् निर्बाधे कुर्वीत विड् वै मरुतस् । भागधेयेनैवैनाञ् छमयति । एकविंशतिनिर्बाधो भवति । एकविंशतिर् वै मारुता गणास् । यद् एकविंशतिनिर्बाधस् । निर्बाधैर् एवैषां निर्बाधान् वृङ्क्ते । ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् वैश्वदेवं द्वादशकपालं सजातकामः क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो वैश्वदेवीर् इमाः प्रजाः क्षत्रायैव विशम् अनुनियुनक्ति । ऐन्द्रस्यावदायाथ वैश्वदेवस्योभे अवदाने अवद्येद् अथैन्द्रस्य क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो वैश्वदेवीर् इमाः प्रजाः क्षत्रेणैव विशम् उभयतः परिगृह्णाति । ऐन्द्री वैश्वदेववर्णे याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतस् समृद्ध्यै । उपचाय्यपृडं हिरण्यं दक्षिणा सजातान् एवास्मा उपदधाति तद् एतद् अनुवर्त्म नाम हविस् सजातान् एवास्मा अनुवर्त्मनः करोति सौम्यं श्यामाकं चरुं निर्वपेत् सोमवामी । इन्द्रो वै त्वष्टुस् सोमम् अनुपहूतो ऽपिबत् स विष्वक् सोमपीथेन व्यार्ध्यत तस्मात् सोमो नानुपहूतेन पातवै सोमपीथेन व्यर्धुको भवति स यत् परावमीत् ते श्यामाकास् । एष वाव स सोमपीथो यच् छ्यामाकस् समक्षम् एव सोमपीथम् अवरुन्द्धे सौमेन्द्रः कार्यस् । इन्द्रियेण वा एष सोमपीथेन व्यृध्यते यस् सोमं वमिति सौम्यो ब्राह्मणो देवतया । इन्द्रियम् अस्य सोमपीथो यत् सौमेन्द्रस् । इन्द्रियेणैवैनं सोम्पीथेन समर्धयति । अधृतो वा एतस्मिन् सोमपीथो यस् सोमं वमिति तण्डुलान् उच्छिंषेत् तान् क्वथति प्रत्यावपेत् सोमपीथम् एवास्मिन् दाधार । अग्नये ज्योतिष्मते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् सौर्यं चरुम् अग्नये ज्योतिष्मत उपरिष्टाद् अष्टाकपालं चक्षुष्कामस् । अग्नेर् वै मनुष्या नक्तं चक्षुषा पश्यन्ति सूर्यस्य दिवा तौ चक्षुषः प्रदातारौ ता एव भागधेयेनोपधावति ता अस्मै चक्षुः प्रयच्छतस् । यत् समानी देवता द्वेधा क्रियते तस्मात् समानं सच् चक्षुर् द्वेधा तस्मात् समानी याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतस् सौर्यस्य मध्यतो ऽवद्यति । इदम् एव तेन करोति यद् इदम् अन्तरा चक्षुषी चक्षुषोर् व्यावृत्त्यै त्रीन् पिण्डान् प्रयच्छति । उद् उ त्यं जातवेदसम् अयुक्त सप्त शुन्ध्युवस् सप्त त्वा हरितो रथ इति चक्षुर् एवास्मै तत् प्रयच्छति यद् एव तस्य तत् सैषा राजनी नामेष्टिस् । एतया ह वै रजनं कौणेयं क्रतुजिज्जानकिश् चक्षुष्कामं याजयांचकार तयैतया चक्षुष्काम एव यजेत । आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं बार्हस्पत्यम् अष्टाकपालं बुभूषन् । इन्द्रो वा अधृतश् शिथिल इवामन्यत सो ऽग्नौ चैव बृहस्पतौ चानाथत तम् एतयेष्ट्यायाजयताम् । यद् आग्नेयस् तेज एवास्मिंस् तेन पुरस्ताद् अधत्ताम् । यद् ऐन्द्रस् । इन्द्रियम् एवास्मिंस् तेन मध्यतो ऽधत्ताम् । यद् बार्हस्पत्यस् । उपरिष्टाद् एवास्मिंस् तेन ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अधत्ताम् । ततो वै सो ऽभवत् । एतया यजेत बुभूषन् यद् आग्नेयस् तेजो वा अग्निस् तेज एव तेन पुरस्ताद् धत्ते यद् ऐन्द्रस् । इन्द्रियं वा इन्द्रस् । इन्द्रियम् एव तेन मध्यतो धत्ते यद् बार्हस्पत्यस् । ब्रह्म वै बृहस्पतिस् । उपरिष्टाद् एव तेन ब्रह्मवर्चसं धत्ते भवत्य् एव । ऐन्द्र इतरयोर् नाभी समादधाति । इन्द्रियम् एवास्मिन् मध्यतस् समादधाति । ऐन्द्रो मध्ये भवत्य् अभित इतरौ तेजो वा अग्निर् इन्द्रियम् इन्द्रो ब्रह्म बृहस्पतिस् तेजसा चैव ब्रह्मवर्चसेन चेन्द्रियम् उभयत आत्मन् परिगृह्णाति त्रिवतीर् याज्यानुवाक्या भवन्ति समृद्ध्यै तद् एतत् त्रिधातु नाम हविस् त्रीणि हि स तेन वीर्याण्य् अधत्त ।
11.1.m:
One should offer a caru to the Maruts; its cover should be a golden ornament with twenty-one bosses; cutting off [a portion of it], one should make an offering if the commonalty oppresses a nobleman.
The Maruts, indeed, are the commonalty.
With their own share he appeases them.
It has twenty-one bosses.
Twenty-one, indeed, are the troops of the Maruts.
In that it has twenty-one bosses,
he wards off their oppressions with the bosses.
One who desires relatives should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra, and a cake on twelve potsherds to the Viśve Devas.
Indra is the nobility, and these subjects belong to the Viśve Devas.
He attaches the commonalty to the nobility.
Having cut off [the portion] of the [cake] for Indra, he should then cut off both portions of the [cake] for the Viśve Devas, and then [the portion] of the [cake] for Indra.
Indra is the nobility, and these subjects belong to the Viśve Devas.
With the nobility he encloses the commonalty on both sides.
The invitatory and offering verses are addressed to Indra and have the form of the Viśve Devas,
for prosperity.
Gold laid upon the [fire-pit] is the sacrificial fee;
he places his relatives close to him.
This is the oblation named Anuvartma ('following').
He makes his relatives follow him.
One who vomits Soma should offer a caru of millet to Soma.
Indra drank the Soma of Tvaṣṭṛ uninvited.
He was completely deprived of the Soma-drinking.
Therefore Soma must not be drunk by one who is uninvited;
he becomes deprived of the Soma-drinking.
What he vomited up, that became the millet plants.
This millet is indeed that Soma-drinking.
He directly obtains the Soma-drinking.
It should be made for Indra and Soma.
He who vomits Soma is deprived of his sensory power [and] the Soma-drinking.
The Brahmin belongs to Soma by deity.
His sensory power is the Soma-drinking, in that it belongs to Indra and Soma.
With sensory power, with the Soma-drinking he makes him prosper.
The Soma-drinking is not retained in him who vomits Soma.
He should leave some rice grains over;
he should throw them back [into the pot] while it boils;
he retains the Soma-drinking in him.
One who desires eyesight should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Jyotiṣmat, a caru to Sūrya, and afterwards a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Jyotiṣmat.
By night, indeed, men see with the eye of Agni,
by day with that of Sūrya.
Those two are the bestowers of eyesight.
He approaches those two with their share;
those two grant him eyesight.
In that the same deity is treated twice, therefore the single eye is twofold.
Therefore the invitatory and offering verses are the same.
He cuts off [the portion] from the middle of the [caru] for Sūrya.
He thereby makes this:
that which is here between the eyes,
for the separation of the eyes.
He gives three balls [of food],
with: 'Up that all-knowing…', 'The seven bright ones harnessed…', 'The seven yellow steeds [bear] you on the chariot…'.
He gives him that eyesight which is his.
This is the sacrifice named Rājanī.
With this Kratujit Jānaki made Rajana Kauṇeya sacrifice when he was desirous of eyesight.
With this he who desires eyesight should sacrifice.
One who desires to thrive should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra, and a cake on eight potsherds to Bṛhaspati.
Indra, indeed, felt unsupported, as if loosened.
He sought protection with Agni and Bṛhaspati;
the two made him sacrifice with this offering.
In that there is [a cake] for Agni,
they placed fiery energy in him with that in front.
In that there is [a cake] for Indra,
they placed sensory power in him with that in the middle.
In that there is [a cake] for Bṛhaspati,
they placed the splendour of Brahman in him with that from above.
Then indeed he thrived.
He who desires to thrive should sacrifice with this.
In that there is [a cake] for Agni—
Agni is fiery energy—
he places fiery energy in him with that in front.
In that there is [a cake] for Indra—
Indra is sensory power—
he places sensory power in him with that in the middle.
In that there is [a cake] for Bṛhaspati—
Bṛhaspati is Brahman—
he places the splendour of Brahman in him with that from above.
He indeed thrives.
The [cake] for Indra joins the navels of the other two;
he joins sensory power in him in the middle.
The [cake] for Indra is in the middle, the other two on either side.
Agni is fiery energy, Indra is sensory power, Bṛhaspati is Brahman;
with fiery energy and with the splendour of Brahman he encloses sensory power on both sides in himself.
The invitatory and offering verses contain the word 'three',
for prosperity.
This is the oblation named Tridhātu ('threefold'),
for with it he assumed three heroic powers.

One whose gold has been carried off or hidden, or who desires, 'May I find gold,' should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, a cake on eight potsherds to Savitṛ, barley gruel to Vāyu, and a cake on one potsherd to the Earth.
Agni, indeed, in the beginning found gold.
In regard to it, Savitṛ and [Vāyu] took counsel.
There is nothing that is not reached by Vāyu from here.
In this [Earth] they find it.
In this [Earth] they purify [it].
In that there is [a cake] to Agni, [it is] for finding [it];
for [they say], 'He is Jātavedas.'
[The cake] to Savitṛ is for impulsion.
[The gruel] to Vāyu is for bringing [it] here.
In this [Earth] they find it.
In this [Earth] they purify [it].
These deities, indeed, rule over gold.
He runs toward those very [deities] with their share;
they give him gold.
When he finds gold, then he should offer this very [sacrifice].
Those very deities who give him gold he makes share-possessing,
for the non-injury of himself.
One should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, and a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra.
Curd, honey, ghee, parched grains, and husked rice grains: that should be mixed together.
One who desires cattle should sacrifice with that.
[The cake] to Agni is for prosperity.
In that there is [a cake] to Indra,
Indra is the giver of cattle.
He runs toward him with his share;
he gives him cattle.
In that it is mixed,
cattle, indeed, are mixed.
He wins cattle.
It should be made for Indra;
Indra is the giver of cattle.
If he should make two offerings together to Indra, it would be a tautology.
It should be made for Prajāpati.
Prajāpati is the womb of cattle;
he generates them from their own womb.
Prajāpati is the giver;
he runs toward him with his share;
he gives him cattle.
The Revatī [verses are] the offering and invitatory verses of the mixed [offering], the Śakvarī [verses] of the other.
Cattle, indeed, are Revatī; cattle are Śakvarī.
He wins cattle.
These mixed ones are five; the other two are [two].
They are seven.
The Śakvarī has seven feet;
cattle belong to the Śakvarī.
He wins cattle.
It also becomes a Paṅkti;
man is fivefold.
Becoming complete, he approaches cattle.
There is ghee.
Ghee, indeed, belongs to Agni;
Agni is the scatterer;
through it he scatters forth.
There is honey.
Honey, indeed, belongs to Soma;
Soma is the placer of semen;
through it he places semen.
There are parched grains and husked rice grains.
Parched grains, indeed, are the form of the day; husked rice grains, of the night.
Cattle are born in accordance with day and night;
for they are born either by night or by day.
He generates them in accordance with day and night.
There is curd.
Cattle have this form,
namely curd.
He wins cattle of similar form.
Honey should not be offered.
Honey, indeed, is life.
